body:
m1 - taking the blend bead, and the FIRST thing I did narrowed it and corrected my own framing. Design proposal on bd-01M177SHFXZKMR8K39BPC9K6FF; no candidate, as I said.

I WITHDRAW "13 CELLS COMPARED AGAINST 13". It implied a source-versus-source defect that does not exist. Measured: PRESENT-TERM SETS ARE UNIFORM WITHIN EVERY ROW - one non-empty set per unit, because the absence conditions (empty sensoryTerms, empty specified) are properties of the RECALL UNIT, not the node. So the offset is common to every source state in a row and CANCELS in the softmax; and since every Viterbi path traverses every unit, it cancels there too. The posterior is not corrupted the way I implied.

THE REAL DEFECT IS SOURCE VERSUS EXTERNAL:

  source cell   = sum over PRESENT terms + prior     shrinks when a term is absent
  external cell = externalFloor, a FLAT CONSTANT     does not move at all (cost.scala:703-706)

A UNIT WE COULD MEASURE ON FEWER DIMENSIONS LOOKS MORE ANCHORABLE. u1 and u2 sit at present-weight 3.200 against u0 and u3 at 3.350, so their source cells are up to 0.15 cheaper against an external floor that did not move. That is exactly what my d_ent run showed behaviourally - Stephen King gaining source mass - and I had the mechanism half right and the location wrong.

PROPOSAL: the blend becomes a WEIGHTED MEAN over present terms rather than a sum.

AND I HAVE TO SAY PLAINLY THAT THIS REVERSES ME. An hour ago I called renormalisation "imputation by another name" and listed it as the option I liked least. I was wrong, and the distinction is the comparison target: renormalising a RESIDUE invents evidence because nothing anchors it; here the cost is compared against a FIXED constant, so a sum whose term count varies against a target that does not is the ratio-of-sums defect we have spent the day removing from estimands - now found in the cost model. A mean is the fix, and it is the same fix I applied to compression and specificity.

WHAT I WILL NOT GUESS: it rescales every cost, so externalFloor, externalMismatch, distortionPenalty and the function priors are all in the wrong units afterwards and need recalibration - and WOG's tuned weights were chosen against the sum. Also whether the prior belongs inside or outside the normalisation. That is a much bigger change than one line.

So: mean-versus-sum, or carry support alongside the value in the MassRatio shape? They are different implementations and I would rather build one than start both. Your call and I will follow it.
